# Business proposal #2: Revisa for Centres

Status: **approved by founder** · Mate's recommendation: **VALIDATE CAREFULLY**

> A simple revision-session schedule and attendance tracker for small tutoring centres in Egypt.

## Problem
Small tutoring centres plan exam-season revision sessions across teachers, subjects and student groups on paper sheets and WhatsApp messages; clashes and missed sessions are discovered late. (ASSUMPTION from the founder's contacts at one centre; not yet confirmed by interviews.)

## Target customer
Owners and coordinators of small tutoring centres (roughly 3–15 teachers) in Greater Cairo preparing students for exams.

## Proposed solution
A browser-based tool to schedule revision sessions by subject, teacher and group, mark attendance, and export the week's plan — no installation and no student accounts in the first version.

## Founder–idea fit (heuristic 4/5)
Can build a records-style web tool with current skills, knows exam-season pressure first-hand, and has two teacher contacts at one centre. Gap: no experience selling to businesses.

## Unique value proposition
See the whole exam-season revision plan and attendance in one place instead of across paper sheets and chat groups.

## Business model and revenue streams
Subscription paid by the centre (B2B); price to be tested; free pilot for the first centres.

- Monthly subscription per centre (price untested)

## Main expenses (all ASSUMPTION unless marked)
| Item | Estimate | Basis |
|---|---|---|
| Domain and basic hosting | 1,200 EGP per year — ASSUMPTION | Rough assumption; prices not retrieved. |
| Leaflets for centre visits | 800 EGP one-time — ASSUMPTION | Rough assumption. |
| Transport for centre visits | 1,500 EGP first 3 months — ASSUMPTION | Rough assumption for about 15 visits. |

Estimated start-up capital: 4,000 EGP first 3 months — ASSUMPTION. Sum of the assumed expenses plus a contingency of about EGP 500.

## Competitive alternatives
- **WhatsApp** — Groups used to announce sessions (status quo). *(named in debate; existence checked in Phase 1 research)*
- **Google Sheets** — Free spreadsheets some centres may already use. *(named in debate; existence checked in Phase 1 research)*
- **Paper schedules** — Printed weekly plans on the centre wall. *(named in debate; existence checked in Phase 1 research)*

## Major risks
- Owners may not see clashes as a problem worth paying for.
- Selling to businesses may take more than 15 hours a week.
- Coordinators may not keep attendance up to date.
- Only one centre is reachable through current contacts.

## Missing evidence
- How many small tutoring centres exist in the target area (UNKNOWN)
- Whether owners already pay for any software
- What price owners would accept
- How often scheduling clashes actually happen

## First validation experiment
**Owner interest test** — Show a one-page landing page and a 10-minute walkthrough to centre owners; count owners who request a free pilot.
Target: **5 pilot requests from centre owners within 21 days** (declared before any results). Five owner requests in three weeks would show interest beyond the founder's personal contacts.

## Reasons for
- The payer already spends money on revision.
- Small, buildable scope.
- Founder has a warm introduction to one centre.

## Reasons against
- B2B sales are slow.
- Status quo (paper and WhatsApp) is free and familiar.
- Evidence so far is one centre.

## Recommended next action
Interview 5–8 centre owners using the Mom Test and run the owner interest test before writing product code.
